newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl urges deputies to approve Czech-German accord.
newsitem.headline: Kohl urges deputies to approve Czech-German accord.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl called on parliamentarians on Thursday to approve a German-Czech post-war reconciliation accord signed last week in Prague which he said was important for lasting peace in Europe.

Deputies were set to vote on the agreement which includes Bonn's sorrow for the 1938-45 Nazi occupation of the Czech lands and Prague's regret at the post-war expulsion of around 2.5 million ethnic Germans.
Bonn parliamentary parties have said they would support the document and were expected to ratify it in a vote later on Thursday.

"It is not a matter of saying that this episode of our history has been put to rest. It was and is about speaking openly about those issues, which could make our common future difficult," Kohl told deputies in a parliamentary debate.

"This declaration should however -- with all respect to hurt feelings -- make a contribution to reconciliation. It should help to break out of the vicious circle of settling scores and mutual recriminations," Kohl said.
Kohl also called on the Sudeten Germans, who were expelled from the Czech lands, and their families to accept the accord.

He also called for support from the political mentors of ethnic German expellees in his own Christian Democrats (CDU) and in the CDU's sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), in Bavaria where many Sudeten Germans live.

The CSU has criticised the declaration saying it does not include compensation for property confiscations after World War Two. But the party has nonetheless agreed to vote in favour of the agreement which it says makes some progress.
Kohl also said the document would help the Czech Republic to integrate into the European Union.
